cbtc.help.title: CB Computer Manual
cbtc.help.guide.control1: Right click a CB Computer to open the programming screen; sneak-right-click toggles it on and off, and programs only run while it is on.
cbtc.help.guide.control2: Drag blocks from the left palette onto the canvas. A statement snaps under another statement to form a chain, and an expression can be dropped into a white socket.
cbtc.help.guide.control3: Click a white parameter pill to type a value and press Enter to save. Pills with a drop-down arrow open a list: scroll to page through it and left click to pick.
cbtc.help.guide.control4: Inline number sockets (such as the count of Repeat n times) accept typed input, and can also hold a number block.
cbtc.help.guide.control5: On an If / Else block the plus button appends an else-if branch and the minus button removes that branch.
cbtc.help.guide.control6: Right click a block to delete it; its children are dropped beside it. Dragging a block back to the palette also deletes it.
cbtc.help.guide.control7: Rename the computer from the top bar, save the program with Save & Back, and open this manual with the question mark button.
cbtc.help.guide.event1: Ctrl + Mouse Wheel zooms around the cursor, Ctrl + Left Drag pans the canvas, and a plain wheel scrolls the palette. Ctrl+C copies the block under the cursor together with its chain and nested blocks, and Ctrl+V pastes at the cursor. While editing a parameter, Tab completes chat targets and Esc cancels key capture.
cbtc.help.guide.ctrl1: When This Computer Runs fires once when the computer is switched on and is the usual entry point; On Start is an equivalent entry block.
cbtc.help.guide.ctrl2: When fires once at the moment its condition turns true; while the condition stays true, every new chat message retriggers it.
cbtc.help.guide.ctrl3: On Broadcast, When LAN Broadcast Received and When Internet Broadcast Received run when their channel arrives.
cbtc.help.guide.ctrl4: When Channel Signal Is Received and When Channel Signal Meets Strength Condition are triggered by wireless redstone; the latter can also require a strength. Both need the Wireless Redstone Transceiver Module.
cbtc.help.guide.ctrl5: When Typewriter Presses and When Typewriter Long Presses fire from a CB Typewriter. A press triggers immediately and repeats every tick after 0.2 seconds; the long press block ignores the first 0.2 seconds.
cbtc.help.guide.event2: When Chat Text Appears is true while any text shows up in chat (Internet Module needed).
cbtc.help.guide.data1: Forever loops its body until Break Out; each round has a built-in 1 tick cooldown so it cannot lock up the server.
cbtc.help.guide.data2: Repeat n Times loops a fixed count, and Repeat Until stops when its condition becomes true.
cbtc.help.guide.data3: If and If / Else evaluate once and run the first branch that matches; wrap them in a loop when the check must repeat.
cbtc.help.guide.data4: Wait Until holds the flow until its condition is true, and time blocks such as Wait convert the chosen unit into ticks.
cbtc.help.guide.data5: Break Out immediately leaves the innermost loop.
cbtc.help.guide.math1: Number and Text hold constants; Get Variable and Set Variable use computer-local variables that are cleared on shutdown; Hard Drive Variable and Hard Drive Set Variable are stored inside the drive item and survive a move to another computer.
cbtc.help.guide.math2: Join Text concatenates two texts, Real Time prints the host clock, and Time is an amount plus a unit (second, minute, hour, tick, game day).
cbtc.help.guide.math3: Sequences come in four scopes - local, hard drive, LAN and internet - each with add, remove value, clear, count, sum, average and content blocks.
cbtc.help.guide.math4: Math supplies arithmetic, powers and mod (remainder), Compare offers six relations, Logic gives and / or / xor, Round keeps a number of decimals, plus Absolute Value, Negate, Scientific Notation and Random Item From Sequence.
cbtc.help.guide.math5: Angle blocks turn a number into an angle (Fixed Angle). Angle Operation takes an angle on the left and an angle or a plain number on the right, wrapping the result to the circle; Angle Compare uses a tolerance; Gearbox Angle reads a gearbox facing (-180 to 180 degrees).
cbtc.help.guide.seq1: Broadcasts stay inside one computer: Send Broadcast names a channel and every On Broadcast listening to it runs, while Set Broadcast Variable and Broadcast Variable share data between the blocks of this computer.
cbtc.help.guide.angle1: LAN (needs the LAN Module): right click in the air with the card to set an ID and password. The first password used for an ID is registered and later joins must match it. Send LAN Broadcast and When LAN Broadcast Received talk to the network, and LAN variables are shared by every member.
cbtc.help.guide.angle2: Internet (needs the Internet Module, one per server): channels and variables are shared server-wide through Send Internet Broadcast, When Internet Broadcast Received, and the internet variable blocks.
cbtc.help.guide.broadcast1: Wireless redstone (needs the Wireless Redstone Transceiver Module): Send Channel Signal follows the native Create dual frequency rule - channel #1 is red, channel #2 is blue, and both items together form one exact frequency. Send mode can be steady or fast blink, with configurable duty timing.
cbtc.help.guide.broadcast2: Logistics (needs the Storage Link Module): right click a Create Stock Link to join its logistics network and sneak-right-click to unbind. Warehouse Free Space, Warehouse Capacity, Item Stock and Send Package then query and ship through it.
cbtc.help.guide.redstone1: Wireless Display Output (needs the Wireless Display Link Module) writes text to a chosen line of a bound display, and Read Info returns one line of an Info Transmitter written by a Display Link; plain numbers come back as usable values.
cbtc.help.guide.redstone2: Send to Chat addresses all players, and Whisper to Player reaches one player with Tab completion for the target.
cbtc.help.guide.redstone3: Chat blocks only appear after an Internet Module is inserted into the expander.
cbtc.help.guide.lan1: Play Sound picks any sound event and plays it at a volume and range limited by the device (12 blocks from the computer, 50 with the Speaker Module; 20 and 80 on a CB Speaker).
cbtc.help.guide.net: Stop Sound silences the chosen device, and Murmur makes no sound at all: it floats a line of text above the device for nearby players to read.
cbtc.help.guide.net1: Network music (needs the Music Module): Play Network Song starts a named song, Play Song From Playlist starts entry N, and Read Song Name, Artist, Length, Played Time and Current Lyric report the playback state, with lyrics in translation or original.
cbtc.help.guide.net2: The device parameter after at selects the computer itself or a bound sound peripheral such as a CB Speaker or a Lecture Stone.
cbtc.help.guide.display1: Nav Table blocks read its position, its target position, the distance to the target, and whether the target sits in a direction, a bearing range or an exact bearing.
cbtc.help.guide.display2: Line blocks describe the target relative to an A to B baseline, and the bearing block can convert the result into an absolute angle through a gearbox.
cbtc.help.guide.sound1: Control Gearbox sets the gearbox, direction (forward, reverse, or shortest path while rotating to), the x1 / x2 speed step and the mode: continuous, fixed angle, jog (turn while held) or rotate to an absolute facing.
cbtc.help.guide.sound2: Stop Gearbox halts it at once and Gearbox Angle reads its facing. The zero point is marked by right clicking with the Gearbox Angle Calibrator.
cbtc.help.guide.sound3: Set Target Locator Position and Target Locator Position read and write the X / Z of a locator module, and Typewriter Key Down and Typewriter Key Held are the two condition blocks for keys.
cbtc.help.guide.aero1: The CB Expander is placed back to back with a CB Computer, facing it. Right click it to open 6 upgrade module slots.
cbtc.help.guide.aero2: Modules decide which blocks exist: Storage Link, Wireless Redstone, LAN, Internet, Peripheral Bind, Wireless Display Link, Speaker, Music and Hard Drive.
cbtc.help.guide.aero3: The status bar at the bottom shows the connected peripherals and module states.
cbtc.help.guide.aero4: Cards can be taken out of their slots at any time: the matching blocks vanish from the palette, and blocks already placed stay but stop running.
cbtc.help.guide.aero5: The expander must stay back to back with the computer; once separated its modules no longer apply, so take the cards out first.
cbtc.help.guide.logistics1: Warehouse Free Space and Warehouse Capacity report the whole logistics network, and Item Stock returns how many of the chosen item are stored. Click the item pill to open the warehouse picker and search by name or ID.
cbtc.help.guide.logistics2: Send Package ships the chosen item and count to an address; leaving the address empty packs and sends in place. Packages need a Packager and Frogport to be handled.
cbtc.help.guide.expander1: Peripherals such as the CB Typewriter, CB Programmable Gearbox, Nav Table and Target Locator are bound with the Peripheral Bind Module: right click to select and right click again to name.
cbtc.help.guide.expander2: Bindings store position and dimension so they work across dimensions; sneak-right-click unbinds. See the Peripherals page for details.
cbtc.help.device.computer1: The main unit. Right click to program it and sneak-right-click to switch it on or off; it stores one block program, runs it while on, and can play sounds, murmur and use broadcasts.
cbtc.help.device.expander1: Attaches back to back with a CB Computer and provides 6 upgrade module slots that unlock blocks.
cbtc.help.device.expander2: The status bar shows module states once cards are inserted; removing a card hides its blocks from the palette.
cbtc.help.device.types1: CB Typewriter: fires key blocks and can act as a display output.
cbtc.help.device.types2: CB Programmable Gearbox: driven by Control Gearbox, Stop Gearbox and Gearbox Angle, using the Create sequenced gearshift look and drivetrain.
cbtc.help.device.types3: Nav Table: provides position, target position, distance and bearing data.
cbtc.help.device.types4: Target Locator: stores an X / Z target that blocks can read and write.
cbtc.help.device.types5: CB Speaker and Lecture Stone: sound peripherals that Play Sound, Murmur and network music can target.
cbtc.help.device.types6: Wireless display: bound with the Wireless Display Link Module and written by Wireless Display Output.
cbtc.help.device.bind1: Right click a peripheral with the Peripheral Bind Module: the first click selects it, the second names and binds it.
cbtc.help.device.bind2: One card holds any number of peripherals and records position and dimension, so they work across dimensions.
cbtc.help.device.bind3: Sneak-right-click to unbind. Device drop-downs list bound peripherals; the empty entry means no device.
cbtc.help.device.modules1: Storage Link Module: right click a Create Stock Link to join its network, sneak-right-click to unbind, and unlock warehouse and package blocks.
cbtc.help.device.modules2: Wireless Redstone Transceiver Module: unlocks wireless redstone blocks that follow the native dual frequency rule (red #1, blue #2).
cbtc.help.device.modules3: LAN Module: set the LAN ID and password by right clicking, insert it to join, and unlock LAN broadcast, variable and sequence blocks.
cbtc.help.device.modules4: Internet Module: one per server; inserting it joins the internet and unlocks internet broadcast, variables and chat blocks.
cbtc.help.device.modules5: Peripheral Bind Module: binds peripherals and unlocks typewriter, gearbox, nav table, locator and read peripheral blocks.
cbtc.help.device.modules6: Wireless Display Link Module: right click a display to select it and again to name it, unlocking Wireless Display Output.
cbtc.help.device.modules7: Speaker Module: raises the computer range from 12 to 50 blocks, or a CB Speaker from 20 to 80 when inserted into its own slot.
cbtc.help.device.modules8: Music Module: right click in the air to edit its playlist and unlock network music and song info blocks. Hard Drive: stores variables and sequences that follow the card.
cbtc.ponder.tag.computer.description: A console for building programs out of blocks
cbtc.ponder.computer.text_1: The CB Computer is a console for building programs out of blocks
cbtc.ponder.computer.text_2: Right-click the computer to open the programming interface
cbtc.ponder.computer.text_3: Sneak and right-click to toggle the computer's power
cbtc.ponder.computer.text_4: Programs only run while the computer is powered on
cbtc.ponder.expander.text_1: The CB Expander attaches to the back of a CB Computer, its front facing the computer
cbtc.ponder.expander.text_2: Right-click the attached expander to open its upgrade module interface
cbtc.ponder.expander.text_3: It provides 6 upgrade module slots that extend the computer's features
cbtc.ponder.tag.sculpting_hand.descripti: Sculpts living creatures into machine parts
cbtc.ponder.tag.super_blaze.description: Turning blazes into super blazes with blaze cakes
cbtc.ponder.super_blaze_conversion.text_: A Blaze Cake is a very special treat for blazes
Right-click a Blaze with a Blaze Cake and it becomes a Super Blaze
The Super Blaze is a far stronger variant of the Blaze
Fed to a Blaze Spawner, the cake makes it spawn Super Blazes
The effect lasts 30 seconds, then the spawner turns back into a Blaze Spawner
cbtc.ponder.sculpting_hand.text_2: It sculpts the Super Blaze into a Blaze Supercomputer Unit
cbtc.ponder.sculpting_hand.text_3: The durability bar shows the remaining uses, 32 in total
cbtc.ponder.uncharged_sculpting_hand.tex: On a stormy day, place the Uncharged Sculpting Hand under a lightning rod
The lightning charges it into a Sculpting Hand
cbtc.ponder.info_transmitter.text_1: Right-click the Info Transmitter with a Display Link to set it as the output target
cbtc.ponder.info_transmitter.text_2: Then attach it to the data source and pick the line it writes to
cbtc.ponder.info_transmitter.text_3: The link then writes its data into the transmitter, line by line
cbtc.ponder.info_transmitter.text_4: Bind it with the Peripheral Binding Module, then the Get Info block reads line N
cbtc.ponder.speaker.text_1: The CB Speaker sets where the computer's sounds are played
cbtc.ponder.speaker.text_2: Right-click it to open its single upgrade slot
cbtc.ponder.speaker.text_3: Insert a Speaker Module to raise the range from 20 to 80 blocks
cbtc.ponder.speaker.text_4: Bind it with the Peripheral Binding Module, then the Play Sound block uses it
cbtc.ponder.lecture_stone.text_1: All nine Lecture Stone variants work exactly the same way
cbtc.ponder.lecture_stone.text_2: It sets where the computer plays its sounds, with a fixed range of 6 blocks
cbtc.ponder.lecture_stone.text_3: There is no upgrade slot: right-click does nothing and the range cannot be raised
cbtc.ponder.lecture_stone.text_4: Bind it with the Peripheral Binding Module, then the Play Sound block uses it
cbtc.ponder.typewriter.text_1: The CB Typewriter lets the computer read the keys you press
cbtc.ponder.typewriter.text_2: Right-click it bare-handed to start typing, right-click again to stop
cbtc.ponder.typewriter.text_3: Bind it with the Peripheral Binding Module so the computer can read it
cbtc.ponder.typewriter.text_4: Key presses trigger the When CB Typewriter key pressed event, along with held and long-press blocks
cbtc.ponder.gearbox.text_1: Power enters through the shaft: the input side always turns with the incoming rotation
cbtc.ponder.gearbox.text_2: It looks like a Sequenced Gearshift, but only program blocks control its speed
cbtc.ponder.gearbox.text_3: Bind it with the Peripheral Binding Module, then Control Gearbox sets speed, duration or angle
cbtc.ponder.gearbox.text_4: Stop Gearbox halts the output shaft at once
cbtc.ponder.gearbox_angle_tool.text_1: The gearbox's angle is measured from the orientation of its output shaft
cbtc.ponder.gearbox_angle_tool.text_2: Right-click it with the Gearbox Angle Setter to record the current angle as 0 degrees
cbtc.ponder.gearbox_angle_tool.text_3: The zero point is stored in the gearbox, so angle blocks read values relative to it
cbtc.ponder.storage_link_module.text_1: Connects the computer to a Create package logistics network
cbtc.ponder.storage_link_module.text_2: Right-click a Stock Link with the card to join the network it belongs to
cbtc.ponder.storage_link_module.text_3: Insert it into the expander, then use blocks to read and write that network; sneak-right-click a Stock Link to disconnect
cbtc.ponder.wireless_redstone_module.tex: Gives the computer Create wireless redstone send and receive blocks
Insert it into the expander, then pick a channel inside the blocks
Channel #1 is red and #2 is blue; both together make one exact frequency
cbtc.ponder.lan_module.text_1: Joins the computer to a local network shared by other computers
cbtc.ponder.lan_module.text_2: Right-click in the air with the card to open the LAN setup screen and set its ID and password
cbtc.ponder.lan_module.text_3: The first password used for an ID registers it, and later users must match it
cbtc.ponder.internet_module.text_1: Connects the computer to the server-wide internet
cbtc.ponder.internet_module.text_2: No binding needed: just insert it into one of the expander's module slots
cbtc.ponder.internet_module.text_3: Broadcast and chat blocks become available right away
cbtc.ponder.device_module.text_1: Binds peripherals to the computer so blocks can reach them by name
cbtc.ponder.device_module.text_2: Right-click a peripheral to select it, then right-click again to name it
cbtc.ponder.device_module.text_3: Sneak-right-click to unbind; one card can hold any number of peripherals
cbtc.ponder.display_link_module.text_1: Binds wireless displays to the computer by name
cbtc.ponder.display_link_module.text_2: Right-click a display to select it, then right-click again to name it
cbtc.ponder.display_link_module.text_3: One card can hold several displays, and blocks pick one of them by name
cbtc.ponder.speaker_module.text_1: Raises the computer's sound range from 12 to 50 blocks
cbtc.ponder.speaker_module.text_2: Insert it into the expander to boost the computer
cbtc.ponder.speaker_module.text_3: Put it in the CB Speaker's own slot and the speaker's range goes from 20 to 80 blocks
item.cbtc.music_module.tooltip: Insert into an expander · Right-click in the air to edit the playlist
cbtc.ponder.music_module.text_1: Carries a 54 slot playlist and lets the computer play music
cbtc.ponder.music_module.text_2: Right-click in the air with the card to open the playlist editor
cbtc.ponder.music_module.text_3: The card's own id names the playlist, and blocks pick songs by that id
cbtc.ponder.hard_drive.text_1: Stores the program's variables inside the card itself
cbtc.ponder.hard_drive.text_2: Insert it into the expander, then use the drive variable blocks to write and read
cbtc.ponder.hard_drive.text_3: Move the card to another computer and the stored variables come with it
cbtc.ponder.target_locator.text_1: The Target Locator Module stores its target X / Z inside the item itself
cbtc.ponder.target_locator.text_2: Right-click in the air with the module to open the coordinate screen and write the X and Z
cbtc.ponder.target_locator.text_3: Put it into an Aeronautics Navigation Table and the table points to that X / Z
cbtc.ponder.target_locator.text_4: Craft it together with a Peripheral Binding Module card to bind them; the module stays in the grid
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_1: The Lodestone Charm is a trinket that carries its own permanent id
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_2: Right-click to wear it in the leggings slot, or in any curio slot when Curios is installed
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_3: Craft it with a compass: the charm stays in the grid
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_4: The compass becomes a Bound Compass that always points to the charm's bearer
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_5: It works while the charm sits in the inventory, armor, offhand or a curio slot
cbtc.ponder.lodestone_charm.text_6: Place the Bound Compass in an Aeronautics Navigation Table and the table points to the bearer too
cbtc.ponder.target_locator.text_5: The card records the module, and the position blocks read and write its X / Z
